name: Sue Piazza

bio.statement: Gresham's city website says Piazza was sworn in to City Council Position 5 in January 2025, with a term running to December 2028.
bio.excerpt: sworn into office in Position 5 on Jan. 7, 2025

bio.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Piazza lists her occupation as business coach and travel consultant.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

bio.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists work as a real estate agent and owner of Piazza Pizza Manufacturing.
bio.excerpt: Real Estate Agent; Owner, Piazza Pizza Manufacturing

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

bio.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists past roles as Gresham City Council president and Gresham Area Chamber of Commerce president.
bio.excerpt: Gresham City Council past President; Gresham Area Chamber of Commerce past President

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

bio.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists Sam Barlow High School as her educational background.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Piazza says public safety is her top priority, including reducing crime.
positions.excerpt: I'll keep public safety my top priority - reducing crime and addressing homelessness

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement says she would address homelessness without allowing tents and encampments in streets and parks.
positions.excerpt: without allowing tents and encampments to take over our streets and parks.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement says Piazza championed the Public Safety Levy to add police officers.
positions.excerpt: I will keep delivering results just like I championed the Public Safety Levy, putting more police officers

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement says Piazza will press for efficient, transparent city government and lower unnecessary costs and fees.
positions.excerpt: I will hold Gresham accountable for efficient, transparent government, lowering unnecessary costs and fees,

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement says she wants Gresham to be a place where businesses grow and good-paying jobs are created locally.
positions.excerpt: We'll make Gresham a place where businesses can grow, employers invest, and good-paying jobs are created close to home.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists parks families can enjoy among her goals for the city.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet statement, Nov 3 2026)

positions.statement: In an October 2026 Portland Tribune article, Councilor Piazza calls the Vance Property a potential major economic catalyst for Gresham.
positions.excerpt: "This property has potential to be a major economic catalyst for Gresham,"

collection_notes: Piazza is the sitting Gresham City Council Position 5 councilor (term to Dec 2028), not the incumbent mayor; incumbent=false for the mayoral race (Meet the Council lists Travis Stovall as mayor). Her pamphlet lists "Gresham City Council past President" under prior governmental experience. Pamplin results were 2022 endorsements/letters (excluded as endorsements/opinion). Campaign domain VotePiazza.com is printed in the statement. The City of Gresham elections page links a filing packet for each candidate; most are scans or forms with personal contact data, so none were used for any Gresham candidate.
